words.definition: knowledge or understanding of a particular situation or issue

words.definition: to give something, especially money or help, to a common effort

words.definition: able to continue without causing damage to the environment

text: Every year, millions of people around the world choose to volunteer their time to help others. Some work with a local charity, while others join a global organisation that supports underprivileged communities. Although volunteers do not receive payment, most say that the experience benefits them just as much as it helps the people they serve. There are many ways to contribute to society. Some people donate money through fundraising events, while others prefer hands-on work, such as building shelters or teaching children to read. Nonprofit organisations often rely almost entirely on these selfless contributions to continue their initiatives. In addition, many companies now feel a responsibility to give back to their community, for example by supporting environmental awareness campaigns or sustainable projects. Volunteering does not always require a great deal of time or money. Even small actions, such as helping a neighbour or raising awareness about a local issue, can make a difference. Experts believe that these programmes empower both volunteers and the people they support, creating a lasting impact on society. As a result, volunteering has become an important part of modern life, connecting people across different backgrounds and cultures.
